Metal gear servo. 55g. 25T spline. measured 39.9 x 19.7 x 42.9mm
Why I need it: The only actuator in the build. Tilts the pan so the item slides one way or the other
Notes: Measured mine with calipers. Body is 39.9mm not the spec 40.7 and the shaft sits 10.95mm off centre. The CAD is built to my unit

Description: Couples the servo spline to the printed pan hub
Why I need it: A 25T spline has 0.74mm teeth which no FDM printer can resolve. The horn is the only thing that can grip the shaft
Notes: Ships in the bag with the MG996R

the funding request
Deployment compute board. 512MB RAM
Why I need it: Runs everything - trigger capture classify actuate and log. Idles at 0.4W against the 4B's 2.7W which matters because the Pi can never sleep between items
Notes: The one I measured pin 1 on is borrowed from a friend. I need my own for a permanent build

Description: Custom Pi Zero HAT. 2 layer. 65 x 45mm. 1.6mm FR4
Why I need it: Everything between the Pi and the mechanism lives on this board. The load cell amp the ADC and the MOSFET are all on it
Notes: Gerbers are exported and DRC clean. TBD until JLCPCB quotes it. A 2 layer board this size is usually a few dollars for five plus shipping

Description: 24-bit bridge ADC for the load cell. SOP-16
Why I need it: Reads the load cell. A bare strain gauge puts out microvolts which nothing else in the build can see
Notes: Runs at 3.3V not 5V so both its signals are directly Pi-safe. That deletes 4 level shifting parts

Description: 12-bit SPI ADC. SOIC-16
Why I need it: The Pi has no analog input at all. Without this the battery voltage simply cannot be read
Notes: MCP3008 is pin compatible if 10-bit is good enough

Description: NPN pass transistor for the HX711 AVDD regulator. SOT-23
Why I need it: Generates the analog supply that excites the load cell bridge
Notes: SOT-23 pinout is base-emitter-collector not BCE. Getting this backwards ships a dead board

Description: Logic-level N-channel MOSFET. SOT-23
Why I need it: Switches the LED ring. A Pi GPIO cannot drive an LED ring directly
Notes: Any logic-level N-FET rated 2A or more works

Description: Assorted 1% 0805 resistors
Why I need it: Ten resistors across the whole board - dividers current limits pullups and the star ground link
Notes: Values needed: 12k, 11k, 100k x2, 22k, 220R, 100R, 10k, 150R, 0R. The 0R is 1206 not 0805

Description: Decoupling and filtering
Why I need it: Every IC needs local decoupling or it browns out on its own switching noise
Notes: C1 C2 C3 C5 C6 C8

Description: AVDD bulk. excitation supply for the load cell
Why I need it: Holds the analog supply steady while the bridge draws current
Notes: C4

Description: Bulk capacitance at the servo connector. radial 8mm
Why I need it: A servo current spike becomes a brownout without local bulk
Notes: Mount at the connector NOT at the regulator. The trace between them is what turns a spike into a brownout

Description: Connects the HAT to the Pi
Why I need it: The only mechanical and electrical link between the HAT and the Pi
Notes: Header position verified against the official Pi Zero 2 W drawing. Pin 1 row confirmed on a physical board

Why I need it: Every off-board thing plugs in here - load cell servo LED ring break-beam and battery tap
Notes: Seven connectors total. A strip of breakable header covers all of them

Description: Top-down camera. 25 x 24mm PCB
Why I need it: Takes the photo the classifier runs on. Nothing sorts without it
Notes: Mount is not modelled in CAD yet

Description: Pi boot media
Why I need it: The Pi has no onboard storage

Description: Weighs the item on the pan. 80 x 12.7 x 12.7mm
Why I need it: Weight tells you things a photo cannot - a full drink against an empty can look identical to a camera
Notes: Check the hole pitch against the printed block before ordering

Description: Capture illumination. 60mm outer / 44mm inner
Why I need it: Consistent lighting so every photo the classifier sees looks the same. Ambient light in a bin varies wildly
Notes: Retainer is not modelled in CAD yet

Description: Detects an item entering the throat. 5mm barrel
Why I need it: The trigger for the whole sequence. Without it the Pi has no idea something arrived

Description: Pan pivot on the idler side. 22 OD x 8 ID x 7 W
Why I need it: Carries the free end of the pan. Without it the pan hangs off the servo shaft alone and the gearbox takes the load
Notes: Standard skateboard bearing. The bearing block bore is cut for exactly this

Description: Powers the Pi
Why I need it: The Pi never sleeps so this runs continuously

Description: Separate servo rail supply
Why I need it: The servo gets its own supply. Sharing a regulator with the Pi means a stalling servo browns out the Pi and corrupts the SD card
Notes: Must NOT share a regulator with the Pi. The two grounds meet at exactly one 0R link on the board

Description: All seven printed parts including the base plate
Why I need it: Every structural part of the mechanism is printed. PETG because it is stiffer and less brittle than PLA
Notes: About 370g used - 230g for the mechanism plus 140g for the base plate. One spool covers it with plenty spare

Description: Idler flange to pan and pi mount to base plate
Why I need it: Holds the idler onto the pan and the Pi mount onto the plate

Description: Servo mount and bearing block to base plate
Why I need it: These take the servo reaction torque. Everything else on the plate is along for the ride

Description: Pi and HAT to the pi mount standoffs
Why I need it: Mounts the Pi to the printed standoffs
Notes: 58 x 23mm Pi Zero hole pattern. Standoff bosses are 6mm

Description: Mounts the HAT onto the Pi
Why I need it: Keeps the HAT off the Pi so nothing on either board shorts against the other
Notes: 58 x 23mm hole pattern
